subject.title: [Bug]: Secret provider crash-loop exhausts 1Password service account rate limits

question: What startup SecretRef failure policy should OpenClaw own for side-effecting exec secret providers under supervisor restarts?
rationale: Changing this path affects credential-provider execution, gateway startup availability, fail-closed security behavior, and existing operator expectations; automation should not choose those tradeoffs from the issue text alone.

options.title: Generic bounded startup policy
options.body: Add an owner-approved generic retry/backoff or circuit-breaker policy for startup SecretRef resolution, keep fail-closed semantics after the bound, and document supervisor restart guidance.

options.title: Degraded startup semantics
options.body: Keep the gateway online when only non-required credential surfaces fail, but require a broader design for which SecretRefs are startup-critical and how operators see disabled providers.

options.title: Docs and plugin resolver path
options.body: Keep runtime fail-fast behavior and direct users toward supervisor StartLimit settings plus ClawHub/plugin-backed caching resolvers for external vaults.

recommendation.title: Generic bounded startup policy
recommendation.body: Add an owner-approved generic retry/backoff or circuit-breaker policy for startup SecretRef resolution, keep fail-closed semantics after the bound, and document supervisor restart guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the strongest feature-history signal for the SecretRef runtime and external provider contract that this policy would change.
